Let \(D_p=(d(x,y)^p)_{x,y\in T}\). We need \(D_p\) negative semidefinite on the codimension-one subspace \(\sum c_x=0\).

Use the automorphisms of the complete binary tree. The zero-sum space decomposes into invariant blocks:

- four leaf-sibling contrast blocks of size \(1\);
- two depth-\(1\) contrast blocks of size \(2\);
- one root-contrast block of size \(3\);
- one radial zero-sum block of size \(3\), where coefficients are constant on each level.

Writing
\[
A=2^p,\quad B=3^p,\quad C=4^p,\quad E_5=5^p,\quad F=6^p,
\]
the radial block, after writing level coefficients as
\[
(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)=(-2x-4y-8z,x,y,z),
\]
is the \(3\times3\) matrix
\[
M_R=
\begin{pmatrix}
-8+2A&-4-8A+4B&-16+8A-16B+8C\\
-4-8A+4B&-28A+8C&8-32A-24B+16E_5\\
-16+8A-16B+8C&8-32A-24B+16E_5&8A-128B+16C+32F
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The first loss of negative semidefiniteness occurs when \(-M_R\) becomes singular. Its determinant is \(64\Phi(p)\), where
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Phi(p)=&-24-4\cdot2^p+64\cdot3^p+104\cdot4^p-64\cdot5^p-72\cdot6^p\\
&-13\cdot8^p+8\cdot9^p+88\cdot10^p-160\cdot12^p+96\cdot15^p\\
&-100\cdot16^p+76\cdot18^p+16\cdot20^p+172\cdot24^p-32\cdot25^p\\
&-80\cdot27^p-104\cdot30^p-16\cdot32^p+28\cdot36^p+32\cdot40^p\\
&+32\cdot45^p-40\cdot48^p+8\cdot50^p+8\cdot54^p-16\cdot60^p+8\cdot64^p .
\end{aligned}
\]
This function has its first positive zero at
\[
\rho=1.374313554912587\ldots
\]
and all other invariant blocks remain negative definite there. The next possible block failures occur later, so
\[
\wp=\rho.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), only the radial block has a kernel, and its kernel is one-dimensional because the other principal minors of \(-M_R\) are still positive. Hence
\[
\dim E=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{(\wp,\dim E)=\left(1.374313554912587\ldots,\ 1\right)}
\]
